description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs:77-87

```rust
/// Returns true if this account supports the given JMAP object type.
///
/// Called by the server consumer (e.g. the session capability builder) —
/// NOT called internally by the handler library. Backends that support
/// all types unconditionally can return `true` always.
///
/// Example: a backend backed by a read-only external directory might
/// return `false` for `Principal` writes, though `forbidden` SetErrors
/// from `create_object`/`update_object`/`destroy_object` are the primary
/// enforcement mechanism.
fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool;
```

The docstring contradicts itself:

1. \"NOT called internally by the handler library.\" If the library
   never calls it, then the handler will faithfully forward
   `create_object` / `update_object` / `destroy_object` to the
   backend regardless of what `supports_type` returns. The example
   even confirms this: \"forbidden SetErrors ... are the primary
   enforcement mechanism\".

2. \"Called by the server consumer (e.g. the session capability
   builder)\". The session capability builder is not part of this
   crate or any sibling crate in the workspace — it's the
   downstream consumer's responsibility (per the workspace
   AGENTS.md \"jmap-testjig\" section: HTTP, SSE, WS, auth,
   capability advertisement are all consumer-bring-everything).
   So the trait is exposing a hook for a consumer-defined
   capability builder that the workspace does not ship.

3. The doc says \"Returns true if this account supports the given
   JMAP object type\" but takes no `account_id` argument — the
   signature is `(&self) -> bool` parameterized only by `O`. So
   it's actually per-backend, not per-account. Yet the doc says
   \"this account\" twice. Pick one.

A backend implementor reading this cannot tell:
- Whether returning `false` has any wire-visible effect today.
- Whether it might gain wire-visible effect in a future revision
  (capability-driven method registration).
- What signal the consumer (downstream session-capability builder)
  is expected to derive from the return value.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: every backend
returns `true` always (both in-tree impls do exactly this) because
the contract is too unclear to use differently. The method becomes
trait noise.

Resolution options:
- If the method is genuinely useful for downstream capability
  builders, document its expected consumer side: \"Consumers SHOULD
  call this when building the JMAP Session capability object to
  hide methods that the backend rejects unconditionally.\" Then
  fix the per-backend-vs-per-account wording.
- If no consumer in the workspace actually uses it, remove from
  the trait. The `forbidden` SetError path is the actual
  enforcement mechanism per the docstring's own admission.
- If keeping it, add a `account_id` argument so the doc's wording
  matches the signature, and document that consumers like the
  testjig must call it during session-capability assembly.
notes: Fixed contradictions in SharingBackend::supports_type rustdoc: (a) clarified 'per-backend, NOT per-account' since the signature takes no account_id, (b) named the intended consumer (downstream JMAP Session capability builder, not part of this workspace), (c) reiterated that the library does not call this method and the SetError(Forbidden) path is the wire-visible enforcement mechanism. The deeper question 'is this method useful enough to keep?' is canonical-shared (mail-server has the same shape) and deferred.
title: SharingBackend::supports_type — purpose contradicts its own doc; not called by library, consumer expectations undefined
